content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the MSA satisfies the WARRANTY rule at the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

| Rule element | Document | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Professional/workmanlike services | 19.1 — "professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards" | Meets preferred |
| Conformance to documentation | 19.1, 19.2 — materially conform to documentation, specifications and acceptance criteria | Meets preferred |
| Duration | 19.2 — 90 days after delivery **or acceptance, whichever is later** for Deliverables; **full subscription term** for Hosted Services | At/above preferred |
| Remedy | 19.4 — re-perform, repair or replace at no charge; if not cured in a reasonable period, terminate and refund Fees paid; non-exclusive for fraud, IP, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims | Exceeds preferred |
| Compliance with laws / no malicious code | 19.3, plus no-functionality-diminution and open-source protections | Meets preferred |
| Disclaimer does not swallow warranty | 19.5 — mutual, implied warranties only, with express carve-out for express warranties, service levels, indemnities and remedies | Safe |

Two points worth noting in the rationale rather than redlining: the disclaimer is drafted mutually (standard and acceptable), and Section 6.2 gives an independent refund path after two failed correction cycles, which reinforces the warranty remedy. Nothing in the acceptance mechanics undercuts the express warranty, and no "AS IS" language appears anywhere in the document.
